references.text: After Jesus' resurrection, his disciples remembered his words and believed. The same pattern as in [ref:Joh 2:22|John 2:22], where the disciples "remembered" (ἐμνήσθησαν) what Jesus had said after he rose from the dead.

In [ref:Joh 12:16|John 12:16] it is told that the disciples only afterward remembered that this had been written about him – the same motif of remembering Jesus' words after the events have taken place.
In [ref:Luk 9:22|Luke 9:22] Jesus predicted his suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day. It is precisely these words (ῥήματα) that the women now remember at the empty tomb.
Jesus told his disciples to keep his words in their hearts in [ref:Luk 9:44|Luke 9:44]: "The Son of Man will be handed over into human hands." These are among the words the women now recall.
In [ref:Luk 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33] Jesus again predicted his suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day. The women now remember these prophecies that have been fulfilled.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 24:6-7|Luke 24:6-7], where the angels remind the women of what Jesus said while he was still in Galilee – that the Son of Man had to be crucified and rise on the third day.
In [ref:Joh 14:26|John 14:26] Jesus promises that the Holy Spirit will remind the disciples of everything he has told them. This parallels the remembrance that occurs in Luke 24:8.
